thesis.primaryProblem: Website owners need to decide which Search, AI-search and agent-web improvements actually help a useful site become easier to find, use, cite and verify.
thesis.primaryAudience: Website owners and maintainers who can change a public site.
thesis.usefulOutcome: Choose a bounded evidence-backed improvement, implement it safely, verify the surface and measure the outcome separately.
thesis.distinctEvidence: Source-backed practices, explicit hypotheses, reproducible audits, Resolver observations, evidence receipts, experiments and dogfood on real sites.
thesis.primaryAction: Run a focused audit or choose the next evidence-backed change.

in: content usefulness, evidence and citation support
out: a proprietary manifest intended to replace native web standards

problemLanes.label: Be found
problemLanes.job: Help people, crawlers and agents reach the useful surface.
problemLanes.audience: A site owner whose useful pages are difficult for Search, AI systems or agents to discover reliably.
problemLanes.problem: Useful site surfaces exist, but discovery, identity, routing or retrieval evidence is weak or ambiguous.
problemLanes.desiredOutcome: Make the right public surface easier to discover and retrieve without inventing artificial content volume.
problemLanes.primaryAction: Inspect discoverability and choose one evidence-backed discovery change.

problemLanes.label: Be used
problemLanes.job: Make the answer clear, useful, attributable and machine-readable.
problemLanes.audience: A site owner whose pages are reachable but not sufficiently clear, attributable or useful once retrieved.
problemLanes.problem: A reachable page can still be hard to understand, cite, navigate or connect to the user's actual task.
problemLanes.desiredOutcome: Give each important page a clear job, useful evidence, explicit attribution and a bounded next action.
problemLanes.primaryAction: Review the page contract or select a usefulness pattern.

problemLanes.label: Be proven
problemLanes.job: Separate implementation checks from real outcome evidence.
problemLanes.audience: A maintainer who needs to know whether a website change was implemented correctly and whether it later helped.
problemLanes.problem: Technical completion is often mistaken for proof of ranking, citation, recommendation traffic or conversion impact.
problemLanes.desiredOutcome: Preserve implementation receipts and later Search, AI, runtime or owner outcomes as distinct evidence classes.
problemLanes.primaryAction: Verify the change and attach later measurement evidence separately.

routeRules.note: Primary product narrative and entry point.
Applied pattern and anti-pattern evidence graph linking catalog guidance to reviewed site-specific observations and remediation.
Growth loop, hypotheses, experiments and outcome separation.
Research depth supports the product thesis without becoming a separate homepage identity.
Reference depth, not a first-order product lane.

visualPrinciples: Bright high-contrast identity without decorative clutter.
Strong typographic hierarchy with evidence-led diagrams and visible state changes.
A simple first screen with technical depth progressively disclosed underneath.
Motion only when it explains state, causality or progression rather than decorating the page.

notes: The four internal navigation destinations are the declared contract; the external GitHub link may remain a utility action without becoming another problem lane.
Route families are implementation architecture, not a proxy for the number of problems the site owns.
The Site Pattern Graph is an in-scope applied evidence surface but remains subordinate to the primary problem lanes rather than expanding primary navigation.
Visual principles are owner intent, not a beauty score. Performance budgets require real field evidence and are not inferred from static HTML.
